name: Rein Operations
description: Foundation operations extension; status, synthetic rehearsals and explicitly configured proposal tools, plus the database-backed Slack governance slice for identity status, available funds, Contributor proposals and Board polls.

foundationDb.description: Backend-backed governance slice: identity status, available funds, configured-type candidate and spoken-type-phrase reads, Contributor proposal field collection, proposal submission, Board poll, ballot and result writes, post-result feedback on a proposal that passed, and chat-account identity binding. The Agent holds no database credential and performs no database work: every read, write, identity resolution and identity binding is one authenticated call to the backend service named by foundationDb.backendApiBaseUrlEnvVar, with the caller ID from foundationDb.agentCallerIdEnvVar in X-Rein-Caller-Id and the Agent credential from foundationDb.agentCredentialEnvVar as a Bearer token. The proof every call carries is minted per tool call from the host's own tool context, by relaying the trusted inbound tuple to the backend's ingress relay endpoint; it is never a tool argument and never appears in a result. foundationDb.workspaces lists each approved workspace, its platform and its native channel IDs, and a channel outside that list, a missing current-invocation guard or an unusable credential fails closed with no backend call. Enabling this block registers rein_member_status, rein_funds, rein_poll_candidates, rein_vote_type_resolve, rein_governance_proposal_submit, rein_poll_open, rein_poll_vote, rein_poll_result, rein_proposal_collect, rein_proposal_comment_suggest, rein_revision_approve, rein_revision_apply, rein_identity_bind_start, rein_identity_bind_status and rein_identity_bind_complete instead of the synthetic simulators and the legacy proposal tools. The candidate read names one vote type explicitly, never guesses one from prose, and is limited to the approved Board channel and to current directors; it creates, selects, withdraws and votes on nothing. The phrase resolver matches only the display names and aliases the operator wrote in this block, by exact equality after normalization; it carries no built-in synonym or translation, reports several matches as ambiguous with no type chosen, and hands a type code back only when the stored type table already has it. The field-collection tool is read-only and limited to the approved proposal channel and to a currently active Contributor: it reports the fields collected so far, the fields a submit still requires, and a short prompt to ask next, and it stores nothing and never submits even when every required field is present. Its optional draft token carries the collected fields for one later turn, sealed under its own key and prefix, so it is neither a submit confirmation nor accepted as one. After a result the Board may still comment or suggest a revision on a proposal that passed. An ordinary revision of the title or the summary is accepted and made effective by the Agent itself, with no separate Board approval. A revision that moves budget, location, schedule, personnel or the major event flow is refused until a current director records an approval; schedule is material in the current implementation. Feedback is limited to the approved Board channel and to current directors, who are the voters. Identity binding is the one path an unidentified sender may still use: it starts a bind and returns the website URL, checks that session after the website step, and completes with only the short code the person carries back. The status check can report that the verified address still needs administrator registration, but no binding tool accepts an email, contact, user id or any other claimed identity, and the backend derives the actor from the proof. The legacy Supabase and Slack keys (platform, slackTeamId, environment, supabaseUrlEnvVar, supabaseServiceKeyEnvVar, identityEmailMatch, slackBotTokenEnvVar) are refused: this block names the backend, not a database, and the Agent reads no profile email. A recorded vote outcome, a comment, an approval, an applied revision and a completed binding never reserve, approve or pay money, and no tool posts a message.

enabled.description: Explicit opt-in. Nothing registers while this is false or absent.

platform.description: The legacy default governance platform, for example slack. It is not enforced on a call: the acting platform is the host-supplied message channel, admitted only when it and its native channel ID resolve to exactly one entry of workspaces, so one deployment may serve several explicitly enrolled platforms.

workspaces.description: The approved workspaces, one entry per workspace. Each entry names its platform, its workspace id and the native channel IDs approved in it. A tool call is admitted only when the host-supplied message platform and native channel ID resolve to exactly one entry; a channel the operator did not list, or one listed under two workspaces, is refused before any backend call.

platform.description: The chat platform this workspace belongs to, for example slack or discord. Matched exactly against the host-supplied message channel.

workspaceId.description: The workspace ID on that platform, for example T01234567 on Slack or a guild ID on Discord. It is configuration, not a credential, and the relay carries it so the backend can bind the assertion to the workspace the event came from.

nativeChannelIds.description: Native channel IDs approved in this workspace. Matched exactly against the host-supplied native channel ID.

backendApiBaseUrlEnvVar.description: Name of the server environment variable that holds the backend service base URL. The value is read from the server process environment, never from this config.

agentCallerIdEnvVar.description: Name of the server environment variable that holds the registered Agent caller ID the backend expects in X-Rein-Caller-Id. The value is read from the server process environment, never from this config.

agentCredentialEnvVar.description: Name of the server environment variable that holds the Agent credential presented as a Bearer token. The value is read from the server process environment and is never stored in config, a status, a result or an error message.

proposalChannelIds.description: Approved native channel IDs where a member may ask about their own status, and where an active Contributor may submit a proposal. Each one must appear in some entry of workspaces.

boardChannelIds.description: Approved native channel IDs for the Board; funds reads, poll creation, ballots and results are limited to these channels and to current directors. Each one must appear in some entry of workspaces.

proposalConfirmationKeyEnvVar.description: Name of the server environment variable that holds the server-only key used to sign one proposal confirmation token. The prepare step of rein_governance_proposal_submit returns a short-lived token bound to the proposer and the exact proposal text, and the confirm step refuses to write until that token is echoed back with an explicit author confirmation. The key is never stored in config, status, results or error messages.

voteTypeAliases.description: Optional operator-authored display names for the configured vote types: one entry per stored type, keyed by its lower snake case type code, carrying the human name a member would say and any additional names for it. The read-only rein_vote_type_resolve tool matches one spoken phrase against these names by exact equality after trimming, collapsing internal whitespace and case folding; exactly one match resolves, several are reported as ambiguous with no type chosen, and none is reported as unmapped with the operator's own names offered for clarification. No synonym, translation or closest match is ever inferred, and a type code is handed back only when the stored type table already has it. Omitting the block resolves nothing.
